sentences.text: Every component of the model we build—the embedding layer, the transformer blocks, the attention heads, the output projection—is parameterized by a single Python dictionary.

GPT_CONFIG_124M = {
    "vocab_size": 50257,           # Vocabulary size
    "context_length": 1024,        # Context length

    "n_heads": 12,                 # Number of attention heads
    "n_layers": 12,                # Number of layers
    "drop_rate": 0.1,              # Dropout rate
    "qkv_bias": False              # Query-Key-Value bias
}

sentences.text: The vocabulary size determines how many distinct tokens the model can recognize and generate.
sentences.reason: c3847 states that vocabulary size is a required specification for the GPT model configuration, and the sentence correctly describes its function.

sentences.text: GPT-2 uses a vocabulary of 50,257 tokens.
sentences.reason: All four cited claims confirm that GPT-2 has a vocabulary size of 50,257.

sentences.text: This number is not arbitrary: it is the output of the Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer that OpenAI trained for GPT-2, and it must match exactly between the tokenizer and the model's embedding table.
sentences.reason: This is a plausible canonical fact about GPT-2's tokenizer but is not covered by the supplied claims. Requires external verification.

sentences.text: The context length sets the maximum number of tokens the model can attend to at once.
sentences.reason: c3847 lists context length as a required specification for the GPT model configuration, and the sentence correctly describes its function.

sentences.text: For GPT-2 small, the full context length is 1,024 tokens.
sentences.reason: Both c3490 and c3536 confirm that GPT-2 small has a context length of 1,024 tokens.

sentences.text: Intuitively, a longer context means the model can "see" more of the document when predicting the next token, but it also means the attention matrices grow quadratically.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about the trade-offs of context length.

sentences.text: For this reason, the tutorials in this series reduce the context length to 256 tokens during training runs, so that the code can execute on a laptop without running out of memory.
sentences.reason: c494 states a context length of 256 is used for computational efficiency; c537 confirms context length is reduced to 256 to reduce computational requirements; c1671 and c3830 confirm the 256-token context length is used in tutorials.

sentences.text: The production value remains 1,024; 256 is purely a pedagogical convenience.
sentences.reason: Clarification of the distinction between production and tutorial settings.

sentences.text: The embedding dimension is the size of the vector space into which each token ID is converted.
sentences.reason: c3492 provides this exact definition of embedding dimension.

sentences.text: For GPT-2 small, every token is represented as a 768-dimensional vector.
sentences.reason: All four cited claims confirm that GPT-2 small uses an embedding dimension of 768.

sentences.text: This same dimensionality flows through every transformer block: the residual stream, the attention projections, and the feed-forward layers all operate in this 768-dimensional space.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about how the embedding dimension is used throughout the model.

sentences.text: `n_heads` is the number of attention heads present in each transformer block.
sentences.reason: c3494 provides this exact definition of n_heads.

sentences.text: GPT-2 small uses 12 attention heads.
sentences.reason: All three cited claims confirm that GPT-2 small has 12 attention heads.

sentences.text: Each head operates on a slice of the embedding dimension (768 / 12 = 64 dimensions per head), allowing the model to attend to different aspects of the input in parallel.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about how attention heads partition the embedding dimension.

sentences.text: `n_layers` is the number of transformer blocks stacked in the model.
sentences.reason: c3495 provides this exact definition of n_layers.

sentences.text: GPT-2 small has 12 transformer blocks.
sentences.reason: All four cited claims confirm that GPT-2 small has 12 transformer blocks.

sentences.text: Each block contains a multi-head self-attention sublayer followed by a feed-forward sublayer, with layer normalization and residual connections around each.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about the internal structure of transformer blocks.

sentences.text: The dropout rate is a regularization parameter.
sentences.reason: c498 states that dropout rate is a regularization parameter.

sentences.text: GPT-2 small sets it to 0.1.
sentences.reason: Both c534 and c1676 confirm that GPT-2 small uses a dropout rate of 0.1.

sentences.text: During training, dropout randomly zeroes out 10% of activations, which helps prevent overfitting.
sentences.reason: Explanatory statement about how dropout works.

sentences.text: When experimenting or debugging, it is common to set dropout to zero so that the model's behavior is fully deterministic and easier to inspect.
sentences.reason: c498 states that dropout rate can be set to zero and is a regularization parameter, supporting the practice described.

sentences.text: This boolean controls whether the linear projections that produce the query, key, and value matrices include a bias term.

sentences.text: The GPT-2 small configuration sets this to False.

sentences.text: This is a deliberate design decision that reduces the number of parameters slightly and matches the original GPT-2 architecture.
